title: Parallel Lines Cut by a Transversal
description: Two horizontal parallel lines cut by a transversal, producing the standard eight numbered angles. Serves Geometry and Trigonometry (lines-angles-triangles): corresponding/alternate angles, same-side interior supplementary pairs, and 'solve for x' angle-expression questions.

transversalAngleDegrees.description: Acute/obtuse tilt of the transversal measured from the horizontal lines; bounds keep intersections visually distinct (never near-parallel or perpendicular-degenerate).

givenAngle.description: The one angle whose measure is printed on the figure; null if the stem gives it verbally. All other seven measures are derivable from this one.

position.description: Standard numbering: 1-4 at the top intersection (1 upper-left, 2 upper-right, 3 lower-left, 4 lower-right), 5-8 same order at the bottom intersection.

highlightAngles.description: Positions (1-8) to shade with angle arcs, e.g. the pair the question asks about; positions are unique (renderer validates).

showParallelMarks.description: Draw matching arrowheads on the two lines.

showAngleNumbers.description: Print the 1-8 numerals in each angle region.

notes: Renderer guarantees: the two lines are mathematically parallel (same slope, drawn from one parameter), so angle relationships are exact; the eight angle regions use the fixed numbering documented in givenAngle.position; angle arcs for highlightAngles are drawn at a fixed radius inside each region and never overlap the numerals; transversalAngleDegrees is a rendering tilt only — it does not constrain labeled measures.
